scope: Owner maintenance and private definition publication on macOS using synthetic CVDs and controlled I/O failures.
checks: Initial publication writes the reference and empty history atomically. An unchanged update preserves the reference.
A complete candidate stranded before the reference switch stays outside publication history even when its version is lower than the later active version and its detached evidence remains on disk.
Failures after replacing the reference report uncertainty. The reference that survives contains the current generation and its full predecessor history together.

Protection follows publication order and compares all CVD bytes and all three version numbers. Body corruption, version mismatch and a copy of the current content cannot serve as the protected predecessor.

A confirmed mismatch permits checking older published generations. Missing history, no intact predecessor, a timeout, a short read or an I/O error prevent generation deletion. A change after taking the selected lease leaves the selected directory, sidecar and lease intact.

The legacy reference is readable by scans and stays in place on unchanged updates. The first changed publication, including a change at the same version, records the former current generation and keeps other existing generation IDs protected as legacy untracked.

Current, last verified and leased generations stay protected. Selected deletion removes only the chosen entry and preserves the stored wait. A failed history rewrite leaves the record for a later verified cleanup behind an intact predecessor.

verification.multi_block_digest: Compared the generation digest with the original SHA-256 formula using three synthetic files exceeding two read blocks each.
